podcast.title: Can Rock Revolution
podcast.body: The 1990s was the decade when Canadian rock music "really came of age" with the rise of what is now termed the Can Rock Revolution, which was characterized as a genuine revolution in the music scene. "This was the decade when Canadian rock music really came of age, and much of it with the rise of what's now termed the Can Rock Revolution."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition and Origin
podcast.body: "Can Rock" is a term that emerged with the book *Have Not Been The Same: The Can Rock Renaissance* (1985-1995) to describe Canada's significant contribution to Alt Rock. It represents a "huge burst of new acts" in the 1990s that never ceased, encompassing a broad range of Canadian music from The Tragically Hip to Sarah McLachlan and Sloan to the Cowboy Junkies. "Can Rock is a term that came into use with a book called Have Not Been The Same, subtitled The Can Rock Renaissance, which detailed for the first time what happened to music in this country between 1985 and 1995."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Enduring Momentum
podcast.body: The momentum generated by the Can Rock Revolution in the 1990s "never faded," leading to an "insanely healthy" Canadian music scene where artists continue to make great music, export globally, and receive strong domestic support. "But the momentum created by the Can Rock Revolution never faded."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominence in 1990s Canada
podcast.body: Can-rock was a dominant musical genre in Canada during the 1990s, characterized by a mass embracing of homegrown music driven by nationalism and patriotism. This period saw increased record deals, radio play, and the emergence of a new star system. "Let's try to track down some of the can-rock groups of the 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Revolution of the 1990s
podcast.body: The "Can Rock Revolution" describes the transformation of Canadian music in the 1990s, where a robust industry, funding, media support, and a supportive Generation X audience led to a boom in high-quality Canadian artists achieving domestic and international success. "the Can Rock Revolution of the 90s."
